text:
aj: Quick experiment idea — combine a lightweight launch post + live webinar sign-up where we gate a small usage credit until the user completes their first generation. Objective: increase meaningful engagement (real prompt usage) rather than vanity signups. Draft plan below, want quick takes.

elaine: love the focus on first-gen credit. what's the proposed credit amount? :money_with_wings: also we should decide CTA variants (Register vs Try Prompt).@samir FYI re: inbound routing implications.

aj: thinking 250 tokens (roughly one mid-length generation) — enough to try a couple prompts but low risk. CTA variants A/B: 1) "Register for the webinar" (emphasize learning) 2) "Claim credit + Try a prompt" (emphasize immediate utility). We'll randomize post-level CTA.

samir: routing notes — if we do immediate "Claim credit" we need to tag leads as "credit-claim" and route to a churn-protected nurture track. For webinar registrants, add tag "webinar-reg" and only award credits after they either attend or do first-gen within 7 days. Suggests two experiment arms: credit-on-signup vs credit-on-first-gen.

toni: watch for fraud — some domains will bulk-signup to farm credits. Recommend limit: 1 credit per email + rate limit on API key provisioning. Also require email verification before credit is usable.

maria: for the webinar itself we should prepare 3 short prompt templates to showcase value. sharing quick templates (use in follow-up email + landing page):

```
Template 1 — Starter: "Write a 3-bullet product value prop for an AI feature that speeds task X by 60%"
Template 2 — Role-specific: "As a PM, summarize tradeoffs for integrating LLMs for autocomplete vs full generation in 4 bullets"
Template 3 — Prompt-playground: "Given this user input: <paste>, produce a follow-up question to clarify intent and a 2-sentence answer"
```

elaine: nice, keep them one-liners in subject lines. For the landing post we should include a benchmark blurb: "See 70% reduction in time-to-first-output in our pilot" — need to make sure benchmark is defensible. What metric are we using?

aj: good q. Proposed benchmark narrative: "time-to-first-meaningful-output" — measure median time between signup and first non-empty acceptable generation (as judged by simple quality filter). Success thresholds: primary lift = 15% reduction vs control; secondary = +10% 7-day retention rate.

samir: implementation checklist: 1) landing post + CTA variants 2) signup -> tag assignment 3) credit issuance logic (deferred vs immediate) 4) instrumentation: event = first_generation, generation_quality_flag, credit_redeemed, webinar_attended 5) routing rules in HubSpot/Slack integration. I can own routing and tagging.

toni: messaging tone — avoid "free" heavy language to reduce gaming. Use "starter credit" and describe it as a "guided tryout". Also include verification copy in the modal.

elaine: agreed on tone. I'll draft 3 copy variants for the post + two follow-up email sequences (attendance reminder and credit-nudge). Will share by EOD.

aj: owners recap: aj — experiment owner & metrics; elaine — creative + emails; samir — routing + instrumentation; maria — webinar content + prompt templates; toni — fraud & gating policy. Growth-bot: can you create the experiment tracking board?

growth-bot: Experiment board created: https://rbw.in/experiments/4698765432 — arms: CTA_A (Register), CTA_B (Claim+Try), CreditTiming_A (on-signup), CreditTiming_B (on-first-gen). KPIs pre-populated.

aj: perfect. small ask — put a column in the board for "bench narrative copy" (we need vetted wording for public-facing numbers).

growth-bot: Added "bench narrative copy" column. 

elaine: will post drafts in the doc and ping here once done. If we can get test traffic by Wed we can launch a small cohort before the big webinar. :rocket: 

samir: scheduling note — make sure webhook for "first_generation" triggers credit issue only after email verified event. I'll add that to the spec.

aj: thanks everyone — aiming to launch split test on Wednesday morning PST. If no blockers by Tue EOD we proceed.
